ConnectionStrings.//: The compose container from docker-compose.yml, on host port 14330. CHANGED 2026-08-27 — it pointed at Server=.\SQLEXPRESS, which is a local named instance that exists on one developer's machine. quickstart.md says `docker compose up -d db`, so a clean clone on a Docker-only machine started a container the application never talked to: /health correctly reported the database Unhealthy, and the honest report made it look like a broken health check rather than a wrong address. The password is the same throwaway already committed in docker-compose.yml, so this adds no secret that was not already in the repository — it supersedes `001` AC-10's Windows-auth criterion, which was protecting nothing while making the documented path fail. Point this at a local instance if you have one; nothing else changes.
ConnectionStrings.//003b: TWO strings, and they are different principals (`003b` Q-A). `Wasl` is what the application serves requests as: the restricted `wasl_app`, which cannot UPDATE or DELETE dbo.AuditLog. `WaslMigrator` carries the DDL rights that `--provision` and `--seed` need, and NOTHING reads it at request time — AddInfrastructure refuses to start if the two are ever the same value. Run `dotnet user-secrets -p src/Wasl.Api set "Database:AppPassword" "<a password>"` then `dotnet run --project src/Wasl.Api -- --provision` once. Local development uses the restricted principal too, deliberately: two shapes of connection between a developer machine and CI is exactly how `004` D-6 happened.
